tool_args.rationale: All seven rows have H = 0.6 and the same initial state. Both a saturating endpoint law and a finite-time relaxation law fit those rows within tolerance, yet they can predict different responses away from the observed slice. A finer trajectory can distinguish a single relaxation timescale from delayed two-layer transfer before fresh confirmation.

considered_alternatives.option: Single-state relaxation with drive- and sink-dependent rates
considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: It fits the observed endpoints within tolerance, but the single observation time does not establish the relaxation law.
The bridge note motivates this mechanism, but the current endpoints do not resolve a second transfer timescale.
The acquired rows already show strong sink inhibition; more endpoint contrasts are less useful than time-resolved data.
